text:
maya: FYI found multiple README snippets that literally assign `API_KEY = 'PUT_KEY_HERE'` and then use it in fetch. That's a copy-paste security smell for new users.

owen: Ack. Which folders?

maya: examples/js-widget, examples/legacy-chat, and docs/static/html-embed. The TS example also uses the old package name, which breaks for people using the new monorepo packages.

li: We should switch examples to show the SDK initialization and env var approach. Suggest: Node: `const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })`; Python: `client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))`. Call out using .env with direnv or .env.local (gitignored).

owen: Can we add a GitHub Actions check in docs CI that greps for literal tokens like PUT_KEY_HERE, YOUR_KEY, INSERT_KEY? Fail the job if found.

ci-bot: scanning docs for disallowed patterns... matches found in examples/legacy-chat/README.md

maya: I'll open a docs PR to replace the inline keys and update the example imports to `@redwood/inference`. I'll also add a short paragraph about retries/backoff: "Use SDK options to set retry/backoff to avoid tight retry loops."

li: Also update the docs generator templates in infra/docs-templates so future generated snippets are SDK-first. Add a unit test that asserts generated sample contains `RedwoodClient`.

doc-bot: Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/820 branch: docs/remove-inline-keys preview: https://deploy.preview/820

owen: Once merged, drop a note in #announcements reminding contributors about the new CONTRIBUTING guideline: no plaintext keys in examples.

ci-bot: docs CI passed on branch; merge complete. 8 files updated.

maya: I'll follow up with a quick sweep across external example repos and open PRs for any stray snippets. Thanks team. :rocket:
